top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one simple, general mechanism: at the magic wavelength the trap light shifts both clock levels equally and drops out of the measurement. The idea (Katori) and the 1e-18 demonstration (Ye) are understood quantitatively by light-shift theory, have been reproduced and surpassed independently at several laboratories, and already yield physics (millimetre-scale redshift, limits on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings). The two-name credit is the one every member proposed, and a citation limited to the invention and development of the lattice clock does not re-claim the 2005 comb or 2012 ion-control prizes. The caveats (Lemonde, Takamoto and others not covered) are real but do not justify no award.
